hero.category: Application memory for AI-native software teams
hero.headline: Production memory for coding agents.
hero.tagline: Mark runtime behavior so future coding agents can remember it.
hero.body: Your agent knows the code. Flowmark remembers what happened in production.

steps.title: Connect
steps.detail: Connect the repository and environment. You set access and collection policy. The agent gets one installation change to review.

steps.title: Understand
steps.detail: Start from a ticket, diff, file or symbol. The agent gets the production cases that could change the patch, and what the evidence leaves open.

steps.title: Improve Memory
steps.detail: When a consequential fact is missing, the agent adds the smallest observation in the same pull request and leaves a question the next agent can answer.

steps.title: Verify Changes
steps.detail: The change carries the case behind its test. After release, Flowmark checks that distinction on the artifact that actually ran.

loop.heading: One agent's discovery becomes the next agent's evidence.

steps.title: Connect
steps.detail: You set the intent. Flowmark connects the repository under the policy you approve.

steps.title: Understand
steps.detail: The agent retrieves a real case and a contrary case before choosing the patch.

steps.title: Improve Memory

steps.detail: The next release confirms the distinction, or shows that it is still open.

agents.heading: Runtime context for coding agents.
agents.body: Start with a ticket, diff, file or symbol. Flowmark returns the cases that matter for that change, including a contrary case when one was observed, and the question that is still open.
agents.viewLabel: Explore what a coding agent can read

views.label: Paths
views.detail: Follow the route the application actually took.

views.label: Attempts
views.detail: See where work repeated within the same execution.

views.label: Outcomes
views.detail: Find the result the application reported at the end of each path.

coverage.heading: Runtime memory coverage
coverage.body: Every maintained question says whether the boundary is known, the fixture passed, and eligible traffic has answered it. A missing population stays unknown. Waiting does not become a rate.

items.question: Who maintains the observations?
items.answer: The coding agent maintains observations in the same pull request as the change. It reuses an existing event when that event already attests the fact, and adds the smallest observation when it does not. You set collection policy and approve the merge.

items.question: What is Studio for?
items.answer: Studio is where you connect repositories, set policy, and inspect evidence. Open a citation to see the case behind a pull request, or coverage to see a question that is waiting, stale, or unavailable. Asking Flowmark from the coding agent is the ordinary path.

items.question: Can I inspect the source?
items.answer: Yes. You can run Flowmark locally. The SDK and core are open source under Apache 2.0, and the platform source is available under the Functional Source License.
